newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast gasoline moves lower with NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast gasoline moves lower with NYMEX.

text.p: U.S. West Coast gasoline prices moved lower Monday with NYMEX, while local traders failed to provide momentum as they waited for Tuesday's inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute (API).
"We're still down on the Merc," a trader said, adding that any builds in Tuesday's APIs would put West Coast values in a tailspin.
Last week, the API reported West Coast gasoline stocks stood 29.8 million barrels for the week ended November 8, or 3.4 million barrels over the comparable period a year earlier.
Traders saw activity idling until the release of inventory figures late Tuesday.
Spot gasoline prices for conventional grade in Los Angeles eased 0.50 cent from Friday to 58/59 cents a gallon, following NYMEX gasoline's 115 point drop to 66.92 cents a gallon Monday.
CARB-grade gasolines remained unchanged from Friday at 62/62.75 cents gallon in L.A.. San Francisco grades remained about four cents lower than L.A. materials.
Offers for Los Angeles jet fuel eased by 0.75 cent in L.A. to 71 cents. The products fell following rumors last week that cargoes were leaving the Bay for Asia, brokers said.
Other materials held at Friday's late levels.
